OverviewAudiology is the science of studying hearing, balance and related disorders. As healthcare professionals, audiologist specialize in “prevention, identification, diagnoses, and evidence-based treatment of hearing, balance, and other auditory disorders for people of all ages” (ASHA, 2021). Utilizing different assessment techniques, audiologists reach a decision as to whether someone’s sensitivity to sound is within normal physiological levels. In contrast, if it is determined not to be so (i.e., a hearing loss is present), audiologists, through a series of meticulous testing, identify the location of the hearing loss (outer/middle/inner ears, auditory nerve, and/or central nervous system), part of hearing affected (i.e., which frequencies), the degree of the identified hearing loss (i.e., severity), and the appropriate course of action (e.g., audiological rehabilitation, referrals to other professionals, etc.). The B.A. program in Social Work is designed to prepare students for a rewarding career in social services, providing the knowledge and skills needed to empower individuals, families, and communities. This interdisciplinary program integrates theories from psychology, sociology, public health, and law to create a comprehensive understanding of human behavior, social systems, and the challenges faced by vulnerable populations. Students will engage with core social work principles, such as social justice, ethics, and advocacy, while developing
practical skills in areas like crisis intervention, group facilitation, and community organization.

The curriculum is built around a combination of classroom learning and hands-on experience. Through field practicums, students will have the opportunity to work with diverse populations in real-world settings, applying theoretical concepts to practice. The program covers a wide range of social work fields, including mental health, child welfare, healthcare, substance abuse, and criminal justice, equipping graduates with the flexibility to work in various sectors.

Graduates of this program will be well-prepared to pursue professional licensure, further their education with advanced degrees, or enter the workforce in roles such as case managers, counselors, community organizers, or policy advocates. With a focus on promoting social change and supporting marginalized communities, the program aims to develop compassionate, ethical, and effective social work practitioners.
